record.original_question: A topological space X is hyper-sober if for every irreducible set F there is a unique x in F such that F is contained in the closure of {x}. If X and Y are hyper-sober spaces, must their product space X x Y also be hyper-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 1.10. Is the product space of two hyper-sober spaces again a hyper-sober space?
A topological space X is called hyper-sober if for any irreducible set F, there is a unique x in F such that F subset cl({x}).
In Section 5, we will give a positive answer to Question 1.10.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a topological space $X$ hyper-sober if for every irreducible subset $F\subseteq X$ (i.e., $F$ is nonempty and cannot be written as a union of two proper relatively closed subsets) there exists a unique point $x\in F$ such that $F\subseteq \overline{\{x\}}$, where the closure is taken in $X$.

Prove or disprove: if $X$ and $Y$ are hyper-sober topological spaces, then their product space $X\times Y$ (with the product topology) is also hyper-sober.
artifact.status_search_result: The product of two hyper-sober spaces is hyper-sober; this was given a positive answer in the literature on H-sober/hyper-sober spaces, and subsequent works affirm the result.
